labels.note: Removing ^ lets strict protocol regex match anywhere in string, not just at start; e.g. 'foo http://x' now matches.
Replacing \s with \S disallows whitespace inside scheme chars; only affects unusual inputs with spaces in scheme.
Regex unanchored at end; requiring 1 vs 1-2 slashes doesn't change boolean match result since rest is unconstrained.
Dropping ^ makes protocol-relative check match '//' anywhere, causing false positives for paths like '/a//b', a security-relevant check.
Dropping ^ lets script-protocol regex match dangerous scheme anywhere in string, e.g. 'xjavascript:' now flagged/matched incorrectly.
Dropping $ lets script-protocol regex match strings with trailing content after colon, e.g. 'javascript:alert(1)' now also matches.
Replacing \s with \S makes prefix allow any non-whitespace char, letting arbitrary text before scheme bypass intended whitespace-only prefix check.
Dropping $ makes trailing-slash regex match any slash anywhere, so hasTrailingSlash wrongly returns true for non-trailing slashes like '/foo/bar'.
